commit.message:
Show the Home Assistants on the network on the welcome screen

The welcome screen looks up Home Assistant over mDNS while it shows,
every 10 seconds, and lists each one it finds below Let's go with its
name and address. Each opens in the browser. One that Home Assistant OS
still installs says Installing, and one whose owner has yet to onboard
it says Not set up yet.

The new check_ha_onboarded command reads /api/onboarding, which the
onboarding integration serves without authentication until every step
is done. Announcements now carry the location_name they announce.

commit.message:
Open each found Home Assistant where it says, in one row that scrolls

A found Home Assistant now opens at the internal_url it announces, which
says whether it takes HTTPS and may name it as its certificate does. One
that names an address it is no longer at keeps only its scheme. The
onboarding check asks over HTTPS when plain HTTP gets no answer, without
checking the certificate: it sends nothing and only picks a label.

The found ones stay in one row. One that doesn't fit scrolls sideways: the
next card shows in part, the row fades out toward each edge with more
beyond it, and a button there scrolls on. Names and addresses keep their
own direction in a right-to-left page.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Keep focused cards, drop replaced landing pages, fade both RTL edges

The found cards are keyed by address, so a card keeps its element, and
with it the focus and where it opens, when another one sorts before it.

A landing page is forgotten once Home Assistant answers on the same
device, on whatever port: newer landing pages answer on port 80, Home
Assistant on 8123, and the landing page's announcement can linger.

Midway along a right-to-left row both edges fade: the rule for both
edges now comes last and is as specific as the right-to-left ones.

commit.message:
Open a proxied Home Assistant at its proxy, and wrap long addresses

An internal_url on another IP address than Home Assistant's own can be a
proxy in front of it, so it is opened as announced. Only one this
computer can't reach, like Home Assistant OS's own networks, gives way to
plain HTTP at the address Home Assistant answers at.

A long name a card opens at breaks within the card, rather than running
over its icon and out of it.

commit.message:
Look Home Assistant up through macOS's own Bonjour

On macOS the lookup sent mDNS queries of its own beside mDNSResponder,
which owns the mDNS port there, and got no answers, while `dns-sd -B
_home-assistant._tcp` listed Home Assistant on the same Mac. It now
browses, resolves and looks up addresses through the DNS-SD API in
libSystem, as Windows does through its own. The app's Info.plist names
the service type in NSBonjourServices, which macOS requires to browse
for it. Linux keeps mdns-sd.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JYKnLnxxYRaTX7zfUKL4Xy

commit.message:
Report a macOS browse that fails, rather than finding nothing

A browse that mDNSResponder ends, or that reports an error, now fails the
lookup, so the welcome screen keeps what it found instead of counting a
miss. A resolve that fails still leaves out only its own instance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Look Home Assistant up with mdns-sd on macOS again

This reverts 3e46908 and 681f686. mdns-sd finds Home Assistant on macOS
beside mDNSResponder, in an app bundle as from a shell, once the app has
local network access. The lookup found nothing in pull request builds
because Tauri leaves those signed by the linker alone, as hai_desktop,
and macOS then applies no local network access the user gave Home
Assistant Installer to them.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Sign pull request builds for macOS ad hoc

Without a certificate, Tauri left the app signed by the linker alone, as
hai_desktop, with its Info.plist unbound. macOS then applied no local
network access given to Home Assistant Installer to it: its mDNS queries
never left the Mac, and the welcome screen found no Home Assistant. Signed
ad hoc, as Tauri does with the identity "-", the app is
io.home-assistant.installer and finds Home Assistant once allowed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep no onboarding state another Home Assistant at the address told

A check that doesn't tell kept what the last one told at the address,
even when another Home Assistant now answers there, as one can once DHCP
hands its address out again. It now keeps that only for the same Home
Assistant, by the id it announces.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Test that check_ha_onboarded asks the address it is given

The command forwards to the backend, whose own tests read the onboarding
steps. These check that it asks the address the frontend gives, says
whether Home Assistant there is onboarded or can't tell, and that the
mock leaves only the device it installs to onboard.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Follow no redirect from the onboarding check

The welcome screen asks each Home Assistant the lookup finds whether it
is onboarded, without the user asking. Over plain HTTP that check
followed redirects, so anything on the network that announced itself
could send it on to this computer itself or elsewhere. It now has a
client of its own that follows none, as the one for HTTPS already did,
and a redirect tells nothing. /api/onboarding never answers with one.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Read no more of an onboarding answer than its steps can take

The onboarding check read all a device answered, and any device on the
network can announce itself as Home Assistant and answer at any length
for the 5 seconds the check waits. It now reads at most 64 KiB, far more
than the few steps Home Assistant lists, and a longer answer tells
nothing, whether it says how long it is or not.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Merge remote-tracking branch 'origin/main' into claude/sweet-knuth-v4xypm

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Hide a landing page only for Home Assistant that answered this lookup

A device written again at the same address starts over with the landing
page, while Home Assistant from before is kept through the one lookup
that misses it. That kept one hid the new landing page, so the welcome
screen showed only Home Assistant that was gone. Now only Home Assistant
that answered the lookup hides a landing page on its device.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
